prompt: Implement tournament selection: draw a few random members of a population from a seeded Random and return the index of the fittest contestant. Complete the select and selectMany methods in the starter file.
explanation: Tournament selection gives fitter individuals more chances to reproduce without ever computing a probability -- it just runs a tiny contest. The tournament size is the selection-pressure dial: size 1 is pure uniform sampling, while a size equal to the population almost always returns the champion. A strictly-greater comparison keeps the first-drawn contestant on a tie, and sharing one Random across all the tournaments is what makes a whole GA run reproducible from a single seed.
hints: Track the best index seen so far, starting from a sentinel such as -1 so the first candidate always takes it.
Only replace the champion when fitness[candidate] > fitness[best] -- using >= would break the tie rule.
selectMany creates the Random once and passes that same instance into every select call.
